subject: On-prem gateway ownership + routing check-in
messages:
From: Jordan Li <jordan.li@acmecloud.com>
To: sean_gallagher
Cc: acme-netops@acmecloud.com
Date: 2026-10-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial: on-prem gateway + routing for Redwood private deploy

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Attaching our current on-prem edge diagram and a short list of constraints we have on the Acme side. We'd like to confirm ownership boundaries for the gateway/edge box that will sit in our DMZ and how traffic to Redwood's control plane should be routed (BGP or static routes), plus whether we need NAT at the edge to reach the control plane.

High level:
- Gateway will terminate TLS and allow outbound connections to Redwood control-plane endpoints in us-west.
- We prefer to keep the data plane egress within our private fabric where possible.
- Firewall team insists on explicit egress IPs and a short permit list.

Can your team confirm operational ownership (who runs the gateway appliance vs. who manages route announcements) and provide any runbook snippets we should add to our change request?

Attachment: acme-vpc-gateway-diagram-v3.pdf (2 pages)
Attachment: acme-config-notes.txt (stub)

Appreciate it,
Jordan Li
Senior Network Engineer, AcmeCloud
jordan.li@acmecloud.com

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher>
To: Jordan Li <jordan.li@acmecloud.com>
Cc: irene_choi, kimberly_park, monica_patel
Date: 2026-10-10T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: on-prem gateway + routing for Redwood private deploy

Jordan — thanks for the diagram and notes. Looping in Irene (network architecture), Kimberly (security & compliance), and Monica (ops handoff) so we can give concrete ownership and an operational acceptance checklist.

Quick answers up front:
- Ownership: Acme will own the physical gateway/appliance and the public-facing TLS termination; Redwood will own the control-plane API endpoints and the application-level authentication. For on-prem proxies that we deploy inside your fabric (if any), Redwood ops will own the software/containers; Acme will own host/network reachability.
- Routing model: Preferred is egress-only from Acme to Redwood control plane via a few stable source IPs we provide. We do not require BGP from customers for control-plane connectivity — static routes with SNAT are fine for most deployments. BGP can be supported for high-scale customers but requires a separate change window and announcements.
- NAT: SNAT on the gateway to a small pool of egress IPs is acceptable and simplifies firewall policies. If you want true source-preservation we can plan for a NAT-less path but that requires more complex peering (BGP) and IP allowlisting on our side.

Action items for us to deliver by EOD tomorrow:
1) Example minimal ACLs and egress IP list (Kim will attach).
2) A one-page runbook snippet for the gateway cutover and rollback (Monica).
3) Diagram with annotated ownership overlays (Irene) — will mark which boxes Acme manages vs Redwood-managed software.

Open questions for Acme:
- Do you have a maintenance window in the next two weeks where we can schedule an IP freeze and DNS updates if needed?
- Any requirement around mutual TLS (mTLS) between gateway and our control plane, or is TLS + token-based auth sufficient?

I've attached our standard private-deploy checklist to this reply.

Attachment: redwood-private-deploy-checklist.xlsx

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

From: irene_choi <irene_choi>
To: Jordan Li <jordan.li@acmecloud.com>, sean_gallagher
Cc: kimberly_park, monica_patel
Date: 2026-10-10T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: on-prem gateway + routing for Redwood private deploy

Jordan — a few inline notes after skimming the diagram and Sean's bullets. See below (I quoted the key bits):

> "Gateway will terminate TLS and allow outbound connections to Redwood control-plane endpoints in us-west."

That's fine. We'll note that termination at the edge is OK, but we strongly recommend doing the following in your ACLs: allow only outbound destination ports 443 to our control-plane FQDNs and lock source to the egress IP pool.

> "We prefer to keep the data plane egress within our private fabric where possible."

For data-plane (inference traffic) routing: if you want to avoid double-NAT and preserve source IPs for observability, we can recommend a split-path: control plane egress to Redwood via SNAT IP pool, and data plane routed to your internal NAT gateways that then reach the inference cluster. We'll add a small diagram for that.

Technical clarifications we need from Acme team:
- Do you expect to use IPv6 for any of the egress ranges? If yes, we'll need those announced or added to the allowlist.
- Are there any TLS intercept/inspection appliances in front of the gateway that could break certificate pinning or mTLS? If so, call it out now.

Operational notes (for Acme change request):
- Plan must include an IP freeze window (48h) and a rollback path that re-applies original NAT mapping.
- Health-check endpoints: we'll provide a small set of control-plane endpoints and a health probe URI your firewall can check to ensure connectivity.

I'll attach the ownership-overlay diagram tomorrow.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Network Architect, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

From: Jordan Li <jordan.li@acmecloud.com>
To: sean_gallagher, irene_choi
Cc: acme-netops@acmecloud.com, kimberly_park, monica_patel
Date: 2026-10-11T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: on-prem gateway + routing for Redwood private deploy

Thanks for the clarifications, everyone — really helpful. Quick answers:
- Maintenance window: We have a two-hour change window on Tue 2026-10-19 02:00–04:00 UTC that should work.
- mTLS: Our security team prefers mTLS for control-plane calls. We can do TLS+token initially for testing but will request mTLS for production cutover.
- IPv6: Not for egress — IPv4 only.
- TLS inspection: There is no active TLS inspection in front of the gateway (we removed interceptors for this project).

Next steps from our side:
1) I'll update the change request with the maintenance window and the request for mTLS in prod.
2) We'll supply a short ACL draft (expected by EOD today) and confirm the IPs once you provide them.

Happy to sync again if you want a short call next week (30 minutes) to go over the annotated diagram and the runbook.

Jordan Li
Senior Network Engineer, AcmeCloud
jordan.li@acmecloud.com
